MANDARIN — TERMLY EXAM #19
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: MANDARIN
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In MANDARIN, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Only memorise without using the language
   B. Mix random languages with no purpose
   C. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   D. Avoid speaking to classmates

2. When practising Oral Expression, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Oral Expression.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Oral Expression.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Expression.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression.

3. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.

4. When practising Phonological Awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness.

5. When practising Reading for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Information.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Information.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Information.

6. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
7. In three clear sentences, explain Reading Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

8. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

9. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

10. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

11. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression.

3. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.

5. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.
